verified.coverageNote: 2342 new distinct bounded JDK Integer inputs compare the small integer helper in 19 backend groups. Existing 1226 entry programs include 406 portable programs and repeat in async checks. Fifteen saved-native suites total 31776 runs, retaining historical overlaps. Existing 27851 Double parse strings and 24254 render patterns remain. Full conformance is not established.
verified.api: Native private fields for immutable value/entry wrappers; direct opaque entry leaves with equivalent bounds and a preserved copying public core API; single insertion hash and direct aggregate traversal; signed int32 and path-segment scans without character arrays.

performance.scope: Twelve typed retained-config enumeration/count and enumeration/hash workloads compare current, fixed 0.19 and native Config. Sixteen enumerations per call; construction and output validation outside timing. All variants exercise the same public behavior. Each call constructs a fresh detached mutable set; no set/result cache is used

regression.scope: Ten exact-render workloads, sixteen existing workloads and three retained Double-list reads compare current, fixed 0.19 and native Config. Long coefficients exercise conclusive prefix intervals and unresolved midpoint boundaries; the latter retain the full runtime conversion. Double-list output is compared as exact binary64 bit strings, converted after timing; public getDoubleList calls and list construction occur inside timing. Render timers retain the prepared ConfigValue; Java retains options and JS constructs its options object inside each call and include returned text; source parsing, optional partial resolution and final result-array serialization are excluded. The full baseline JS module dependency tree is loaded from the fixed Git commit. Retained workloads compare real Config methods with native Config; construction excluded, immutable operations/getter transport included, final result serialization excluded. Each workload has five fresh processes; Java legacy and retained workloads use separate processes. Startup, I/O and sustained/peak-memory parity are not measured.
